newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Tung in talks with Taiwan, aides say.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung in talks with Taiwan, aides say.

text.p: Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa launched into talks with Taipei on Thursday, just a day after he had predicted a quick deal on Taiwan's future status in this territory, which returned to Beijing's control this week.

A Tung aide and a spokesman at Taiwan's unofficial mission in Hong Kong told Reuters Tung was meeting Koo Chen-fu, Taiwan's top negotiator on Taipei-mainland relations. China regards Taiwan as a rebel province and is working for the island's reunification with the mainland.

A spokesman at Taiwan's Kwang Hwa Travel Service, Taipei's unofficial representative office in Hong Kong, told Reuters Koo, who came for this week's handover celebrations, would hold a news conference later on Thursday. He declined to give further details.
A Tung aide told Reuters the meeting would take place on Thursday afternoon but refused to say where in Hong Kong they were meeting and what the subject would be.
Koo is head of the Straits Exchange Foundation, the Taiwan body that handles relations and negotiations with Beijing.

Tung, holding his first news conference on Wednesday since taking office, vowed to pursue a dialogue with Taiwan and predicted the future of Taipei's official presence in this new special administrative region of China would be settled soon.
